primitives.name: Brand Lock Consistency Matrix
primitives.verbatim_quote: Set-level consistency matrix Review all outputs together: ```text Asset | Logo | Palette | Type | Grid/spacing | Shape/device | Format | Status ``` An asset passes only when it follows the same Brand Lock.
primitives.assumptions: All assets are evaluated under a fixed Brand Lock; status is binary per asset.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When any asset deviates from Brand Lock, S = false.

layer2.mapping: Matrix of asset-state tuples is isomorphic to a categorical fiber product over Brand Lock.
layer2.telemetry: Boolean vector of asset compliance with Brand Lock

primitives.name: Asset Dependency Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: When logo, typography, or palette approval changes, remove every invalidated downstream element from the active deliverable set.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D': 'Downstream asset set (set)', 'L': 'Logo state (dimensionless)', 'T': 'Typography state (dimensionless)', 'P': 'Palette state (dimensionless)', 'K': 'Kernel of dependency (function)'}
primitives.assumptions: Changes in L, T, or P induce a kernelized removal of dependent assets.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Kernel K(L, T, P) maps to D ⊆ D' where D' is full asset set.

layer2.mapping: Kernel defines a closure operator on deliverable sets under Brand Lock change.
layer2.telemetry: Size of invalidated downstream set post-change

reasoning_traces.think:
The QA process is modeled as a categorical pullback over a Brand Lock fiber bundle, where each asset is a section of the bundle. Inconsistencies arise when sections fail to respect the global Brand Lock constraint, triggering a kernelized invalidation of downstream assets. The delivery manifest stabilizes this process by enforcing deterministic naming conventions that allow selective re-execution. This structure supports both Bayesian inference over asset states and state-transition logic in GSE, ensuring that changes propagate correctly through the system while maintaining traceability.
